title: Your first async method
sub: async, await and where a method pauses
cards/0/body:
async on a method lets you use await inside it.

await takes a task. If the task isn't done yet, the method "pauses" and returns control to its caller. When the task finishes, the method picks up right where it left off.
cards/1/body:
Until the first await that actually waits, an async method runs like any other: on the same thread, with no switching.

And if the task has already completed, await doesn't pause at all.
cards/2/q: What does the caller get when GetLengthAsync reaches await on an unfinished request?
cards/2/explain: The method returns a task right away, at its first real pause. The result comes later.
cards/3/q: On which line can the method pause?
cards/3/explain: A method can only pause at an await.
cards/4/q: return html.Length returns an int, but the method is declared Task<int>. Why is that allowed?
cards/4/options/0: The compiler wraps the result in a task for you
cards/4/options/2: An int automatically becomes a Task
cards/4/explain: In an async method, return sets the result of the future task.
cards/5/explain: async goes in the declaration, await before the task.
cards/6/task: Same async code: run it in WPF, then in a console app. Who runs the continuation?
cards/7/q: Which are true? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/0: Until the first await, an async method runs synchronously
cards/7/options/1: Awaiting an already completed task doesn't pause the method
cards/7/options/2: An async method with no await inside runs synchronously
cards/7/options/3: async by itself creates a new thread
cards/7/explain: async doesn't create threads or block. It's a way to cut a method into pieces around its waits.
cards/8/q: A method is marked async but has no await inside. What happens?
cards/8/options/0: It runs synchronously, and the compiler warns you (CS1998)
cards/8/explain: No await means no pauses: the method runs to the end and returns an already completed task.
